utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are grateful for the time that has been allocated over part of Friday and the weekend for an examination of the two transcripts that we have. In fact, it is been extremely useful and there are observations I'd wish to make in relation to this. Your Honours were in private session on Friday in relation to this, and I don't know whether in order to develop the points I should in fact go into private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Unfortunately the submissions have gone on much longer than anticipated and there is more to come. We must therefore take the first of the afternoon breaks now and will resume at 10 minutes past 4.00 to continue with submissions in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Topolski, private session again, I assume?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: For these further submissions it will be necessary to go into private session again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The submissions from counsel have now concluded. The Chamber proposes to adjourn for a little time to consider the submissions. We will resume as -- when we are in a position to do so. We will adjourn temporarily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are grateful to counsel for the submissions we've received to assist us in the resolution of this application by the Prosecution in respect of the present witness. We have come to a clear decision in deference to some of the detail of the submissions. We propose to simply announce our decision at this point and will in the near future deliver more extensive reasons for that decision. In the Chamber's view, the application of the Prosecution should succeed. If the witness could be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, I'm sorry you've had such an -- a long wait, but you'll be pleased to know we've dealt with the legal issues that were being raised and we're now able to continue with your evidence. I'm sorry that you've had such a delay. Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, I also apologise for the wait. Can you understand me?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I intervene, Mr. Whiting. Simply to remind you of the affirmation that you took at the beginning of your evidence that still applies, Mr. Buja. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher I'm going to show you a document with the ERN U003-3675. Do you recognise that document, sir?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Does your signature appear on that document?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the date is the 28th of April, 2003?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no date.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I just draw your attention to your signature on the side of the page. Do you see a date above that signature? It may be that you have a bad photocopy. I'm going to offer you mine, my copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In which case I'll need his.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The copy that you have been provided was cut off. Looking at that copy now, do you see your signature on the right-hand side of the page?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And do you see the date?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, did you draw this diagram?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: This diagram shows the structure that existed in relation to the points or units that existed around Klecka in May, June, and July of 1998. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not exist in May, June, July. I have explained this already earlier, the period of development of the units of the KLA. I did explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: These units that are identified in Javor, Luznica, Lapusnik, Kroimire, Petrastica, and Fustica, those units or points all existed at some point in June or July of 1998. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This may have been so in July when Jakup Krasniqi was in Klecke.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to show you a portion of your interview with the Office of the Prosecutor when you drew this diagram, and maybe we can get some clarification about this. And before I do that, I'm going to give you a copy of the transcript of the interview in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if the document could stay in front of the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we know if this is the transcript we have, 1 or 2. I assume it's 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It's the transcript that we -- was provided to the Court and the parties. It's the transcript that is -- has just Albanian and it should be attached to the English transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: This one?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I can't see that far.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, and it has only Albanian on it and it is attached to the English, which has only English on it. And for the benefit of the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'd ask you, sir, to turn to page 38 of that transcript. And on -- in the English it's on page 37.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me, Your Honours, I'd like to say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No. If you just listen to Mr. Whiting and answer his questions for the moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, do you see on page 38 about halfway down the question is: "At the time we are talking about, was Fatmir Limaj established at Klecka?" This is on page 38 of the Albanian about halfway, two-thirds of the way down. Do you see that question? And on the English it's at the top of the page of 3 -- I'm sorry. I think I -- that's right. It's at the top of the page of 37 on the English. Mr. Buja, have you found that question?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not yet. But could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes. "At the time that we are talking about, was Fatmir Limaj established at Klecka?" And the answer is: "At Klecka." The question is from D.B., the interpreter, and S.B. is you, the witness. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to play on -- and you can either follow it along -- I'm going to play on the computer -- the screen that portion of the interview and you can either follow it along watching it and listening to it, or you can follow it along on the text as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Oh, we have to switch the -- the monitors have to be switched to Sanction, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: "D.B.: At this time was Fatmir Limaj stationed in Klecke? "S.B.: Yes" -- "O.L.: And was it so that either you or Luan --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the case manager to pause this for a moment because the version we had had the -- what I would hoped was going to be played had the transcript underneath.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might inquire. Is the transcript that is going to be underneath the transcript which is represented in V00-4835 [sic] or the draft translation which, for example, in the area that we're just talking about would have been L0108571? Because just with regard to what has been played there is a difference between the word "stationed" asked by the investigator in the English version -- in the interview and the word "established" which appears in the translation. So I'm wondering which one we're going to have for the benefit as we're reading along. I'm assuming it's going to be the 4385 version. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. My apologies, Your Honour, we're defeated by technology. We'll have to play it without the transcript. We'll have it do it the old-fashioned way and follow the transcript. If we could play the clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, if I may make an observation. If that's the case, then the transcript which is in the draft translation of L010 and whatever the numbers are is the actual English that's being spoken. So there is a difficulty here because apparently as I understand the translation process that occurred - and I'll just use for example what just happened there - the English that we just heard was -- from the investigator: "Okay. And at that time was Fatmir Limaj stationed in Klecka?" To which the answer was: "Yes." The English version that you have has: "At the time that we are talking about, was Fatmir Limaj established at Klecka?" So I mean -- I know this is a minor point, but it may as we go on become a major point if you do not have available to you at the time you were viewing the interview the actual words that were spoken as I understand it by the interpreter to the witness. I'm just pointing that out as a potential difficulty as we're dealing with matters I think of not only detail but interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. The potential is clear. We'll see if it becomes a significant issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: We'll play the clip and what I would -- on this matter, it's the transcript that is before the Court and the parties that is what is being said in Albanian. Of course that will differ at times with what is being said on the clip in English, but we'll be allowed to -- because the English on the tape is what's being translated at the spot. The transcript that is before the Court is actually -- and what is before the witness is actually what is being said in Albanian. And the witness can listen to -- obviously to what's being said in Albanian, which corresponds to what is on his transcript and what we can read on our English translation. So if we can play the clip, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: "S.B.: Yes. "O.L.: So was it that either you or Luan attended the weekly meetings in Klecka? "S.B.: Well, I don't know whether there was a sort of regular pattern of this -- or a definition of weekly meetings. But as -- as long as I -- I had to go there, I need to go there, so I went to Klecka. So I got directly in touch with Fatmir. So there was no regular thing -- procedure. So to go through several steps in order to meet so I would go and see him directly. "O.L.: Okay. In the beginning of May 1998, can you tell me what other -- you call them points, but other so-called headquarters as Kroimire were under the headquarters in Klecka. "THE INTERPRETER: I'm sorry. It was -- there were other points under Klecka also? "O.L.: Yes, similar -- similar to Kroimire. On the same level. "S.B.: Yeah, there were other points as well. "O.L.: Okay. Could we -- if I give you a blank paper, could you do a -- if you write "Klecka headquarters" here. "S.B.: Shall I write it down? "O.L.: Yes. I would like you to make kind of an organisatory [sic] -- This is Klecka. And then if we can have the -- all the points going underneath. Okay. And underneath Klecka, if you can -- on the level that took orders from Klecka. Could you mention all the so-called points that took orders from that. "S.B.: As it was a process of expanding continuously towards other villages as the ranks got expanded. Was in May 1998 that another point was set up here. We are talking about May 1998. "O.L.: Okay. Yes. "A.W.: What is written here then? "S.B.: It's the name of the place. It's a village. "UNIDENTIFIED SPEAKERS: Javor, Javor. "S.B.: Javor. Luzhnice was also a point later, but I don't know whether -- I'm not sure whether Luzhnice was in May -- "O.L.: But you can mention it. It's -- "S.B.: Probably it must have been at the end of May or beginning of June. Lapusnik point, May or June. "O.L.: Okay. "S.B.: End of May, probably. "S.B.: Pjetershtice also, most likely end of May. Fushtice. This is more or less the approximately version. So as a -- with the time passing, so you have more and more -- more and more other UCK points in other villages. So we are talking about expanding further beyond Carraleve gorge. Gerricheve [phoen]. And towards Malisevo as well as. So it was also June and July 1998 that Malisevo and other villages were reached. As far as I -- as I can remember from the conversation -- so to say informal conversation. "THE INTERPRETER: I'm sorry. Can I ask him something? "O.L.: Go ahead. "S.B.: So this Lapusnik point had two subordinate points, so-called Celiku 3 and Guri 3, two other points -- sorry. Sorry. It was because of geographical separation from the main road, this way of setting up these points. "A.C.: Could you draw that in on that diagram? These subordinate points underneath. "O.L.: Okay. And the road between Pristina-Peja is the one dividing these two points? That is correct? "S.B.: Yes. "O.L.: And which one is where? "S.B.: On Klecka side was Celiku 3 and the other side it was Guri 3. So on Drenica side was Guri 3."

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, do you remember that part of the interview?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember even though this is why I have demanded to have a transcript to see the possible mistakes I made during the description. You must understand that this happened five or six years after the war, and after the war a propaganda campaign was conducted, very strong one, which was against and in favour of the war. So I might have been affected by the descriptions made about the war and of course this might be freely described as something that had to do with a development of the units at that time. When I say "point" this is erroneous; that's why I wanted to have a transcript because "point" in Albanian is a very limited place, whereas "line" describes a length of territory and it's used in the military vocabulary and I wanted to describe properly here the liberation war. Because at that time there was not any strategy by the General Staff of the development of the points. It was a strategy for the development of guerrilla units and the horizontal development of these units. That was a strategy then. And here I was, as I said, affected by a propaganda which described the war by points; that's why I have used the word "points" even though for me this was a description that was -- that I made after the war that is referring to points. Likewise, I heard what was said here and I cannot answer to these questions in great length because a long time has passed and it took three months for the development of the guerrilla units.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you some specific questions about this passage, but first I want to ask you about this propaganda campaign. Can you describe more specifically this propaganda campaign that caused you to give these answers -- this answer in the interview? What are you talking about exactly?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about propaganda and agitation campaign which was made through newspapers, interviews, given by various superior commanders when describing the war. Sometimes they focused too much on the hierarchy, overdid the hierarchy, or the opposite - sometimes they played it down, depending on how they looked at it, from what political position they looked at it, at the war, that is, in order to continued their political ends, to realise their political ends. Many of them have described them as points, which was not the case with the strategy of the General Staff. We were told to develop guerrilla units in municipalities and to expand these units. Now I'm speaking -- have to recollect many events which occurred at that time and during this interview I was not prepared to recollect these events as they truly were. So I might have been affected or influenced by the descriptions given to the war after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: This propaganda campaign, can you be more -- even more specific. For example, did you read accounts of superiors describing the structure around Klecka in May, June, and July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I heard accounts by people who not only described the events around and about Klecka, but also they described events in other parts of Kosova where the war had been waged.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, let's -- if we could limit ourselves, please, just to the area around Klecka. Can you tell us which accounts you read of -- that described the area around Klecka in May, June, and July of 1998.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you all the accounts that I --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you give me one account? Can you just remember one account that you read describing that area?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The organisation in points has been described by several commanders who describe not only Klecka but also other parts of Kosova. I read interviews. I even saw this in various books, this form of organisation that never existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Which commanders described these points?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Various commanders. Some were -- like the commander of Lumi unit or Drenica unit, Suhareke units. These commanders described this in this form. I don't want to engage in such a propaganda to create an impression of the organisation that was not so at that time because the points were not a form of the development of the KLA. As I said, it was the form of the guerrilla unit which developed continuously.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, can you name some of the commanders that you read describing the points around Klecka in May, June, and July of 1998? Can you give us any names of commanders who you read describing the points in that way?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the way how it was described by the late -- he was a commander of the General Staff, Sylejman Selimi. It was also in the testimony that he gave here, the organisation of points was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sylejman Selimi was talking about a different zone, wasn't he? He was talking about the Drenica zone.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he spoke about the Drenica zone, but the description of the guerrilla units was described as if they were points. This was not the reality at the time because they were guerrilla units.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You are aware, are you not, that Sylejman Selimi was the commander of the Drenica zone starting in about May of 1998?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know that he was commander of the zone; I knew that he was commander of the subzone after May of 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Zone, subzone. But after May 1998 he was the commander of Drenica. You knew that, right, you know that today?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I know it today and I knew it in June 1998 when the organisation of other subzones started. I knew these things during the war as well. End of June, beginning of July, that he was appointed commander of the Drenica subzone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And, Mr. Buja, you're telling us that Mr. Sylejman Selimi's description of points being created in villages and then later brigades and battalions being created, you're telling us that that's propaganda, that's not true?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the description of points, this was not the strategy of the KLA. It was after the war that these points were emphasised as a strategy of the KLA. Simply, to me these points did not exist at the time because the strategy of the General Staff was to develop guerrilla units of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, you agree with me that you used the word "points" in your interview that we've just played here, right? You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've mentioned that at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I was interviewed, but I could not remember the things as they happened, because to recall those events it's a very hard job because you cannot describe things and events under a light -- under the light of the things as they were described after the war. I wanted to describe them as I knew them during the war and I wanted to describe them the way the KLA was organised and developed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Aside from Sylejman Selimi who described the situation in a different zone, can you tell us the name of any commander who described the situation around Klecka in May, June, and July 1998 that you read? Can you name any?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the moment I cannot remember any other names, but there have been such descriptions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you were interviewed by the OTP, did you at any point in your interview say that these were descriptions that you had read elsewhere and that were not your own descriptions? Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to take you through that passage that we played and take it through point by point. Do you see at the beginning, and again this is on page 38 of the Albanian, there's -- the question is that: "Fatmir Limaj was established at Klecka?" And you say: "Yes, at Klecka." That was true, right? He was established at Klecka?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was established at Klecka; I can't deny that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you agree, don't you, that in this part of the interview the questions are specific to May and June of 1998. That's repeatedly said in the interview in this part. Right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the description of the units, the period from May to June and July was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And it says -- there's a question about weekly meetings at Klecka and you say: "I do not know that weekly meetings were defined." But then you say: "When I had business, that is, I went straight to Klecka, meaning directly to Fatmir." And that was true, wasn't it? During May and June of 1998, if you had business you went straight to Klecka. Right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I described it earlier that at the end of the month and even earlier than that in April I went to Klecka to meet Fatmir Limaj, who had the task to escort me to Drenica to contact the General Staff. And this contact was realised by the end of April. In May that is mentioned here, I had a meeting with Fatmir Limaj at the time as well but this was a social meeting, because by mid-June the spokesperson of the KLA came out in the open and when I met Fatmir Limaj I met also the spokesperson of the KLA who was in Klecka at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, if all you had in May and June of 1998 was a social meeting with Fatmir Limaj, how do you explain your answer here where you say: "When I had business, I went straight to Klecka, meaning directly to Fatmir"? How do you explain that answer?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I went to Fatmir directly because the spokesperson of the KLA was there, and the unit led by Fatmir Limaj, at that unit the spokesperson was there and I met Fatmir Limaj in Klecka when I met the spokesperson of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But here you're saying that you went to -- when you had business you went to Fatmir Limaj. I would suggest that it's quite clear that you went to Fatmir Limaj because of the business, to conduct business. Can you explain that answer?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I went there to do work, to do business, because the spokesperson of the KLA came out openly and it was in Klecka that he did that, and that's why I went there to meet him and I wanted to meet the General Staff. I wanted to meet Fatmir in order to learn where the spokesperson was, and he was in Klecka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, this is not about meeting Jakup Krasniqi and the General Staff; this is about going to Fatmir. What kind of business did you go with to Klecka, to Fatmir? What kind of business, aside from meeting with Jakup Krasniqi which is not mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has not been mentioned here, and that is why I wanted to have a look at the transcript in order to improve it or to explain things about how events went on. I went to Fatmir because I wanted to contact the General Staff of the KLA. I emphasised it in the previous interview that I had business with Fatmir because he had to escort me to the General Staff. At that time it was thought that they were in Drenica, and after the spokesperson came out openly I did not need Fatmir to escort me to Drenica. I could contact Mr. Jakup Krasniqi. He was publicly known now as the spokesperson of the KLA. And that was my business, to meet the General Staff or to contact the General Staff through Jakup Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Buja, you see -- we'll move on. You see that you are asked on a piece of paper to write "Klecka" and then you are asked to tell us who Klecka had under its responsibilities. And then the question is -- it says: "How did Klecka transmit orders, that is to these other similar posts that you've described? Can you draw the posts that took orders from Klecka, that is one level below Klecka?" Do you see that question?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Take a moment to find it. It should be on -- it's on page 39 of the Albanian. It's the bottom of page 37 of the English.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could repeat the question again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes. Are you looking at page 39 of the Albanian?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. Do you see the question where you are asked to write "Klecka headquarters" on a paper. And then the question is: "Can you tell us who Klecka had under its responsibilities?" And then it's asked: "Name the posts that took orders from Klecka, that is one level below Klecka." Do you see that question?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And do you see then that you write -- you write down all the names that are on that diagram that we've put before you, Javor, Luznica. And Luznica you say is: "No doubt in May, beginning of June; Lapusnik in May or June; Kroimire in May; Petrastica." And you drew the arrows from Klecka down to these different units that were established in May and June in these villages. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you have to understand that Klecka is a toponym and I have not given here the hierarchy as Klecka. There was the Celiku Unit there. This is the toponym where Jakup Krasniqi was. And when I speak about giving orders or reporting, I speak about the toponym where Jakup Krasniqi was. And of course every unit or every unit commander had the possibility to go and contact Jakup Krasniqi, who had come out openly. This description -- this diagram -- I have said it clearly here. It's been a very long time -- it has been a long time and I was not able to determine whether these units were created in May, June, or July. I tried to describe here the creation of units, for example in Kroimire by the end of May and later other units were created such as the Petrastica unit; the Blinaje unit, which was some days later than the Petrastica unit; then the unit of -- the Fustica unit which was later in time than the Blinaje unit. So I have described here -- I was not very sure about the time when these units were created.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Jakup Krasniqi made his first public statement on the 14th of June of 1998. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And he was the public spokesman of the KLA, isn't that right, after that date?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the spokesman of the General Staff of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: As spokesman of the KLA -- as spokesman of the KLA, he was not giving orders to posts or units, whatever we're going to call it, in Lapusnik or Fustica or Petrastica or Kroimire, was he? That wasn't his job as spokesman of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jakup Krasniqi was the only member of the General Staff that we could see. So through Jakup Krasniqi, we could tell him about our concerns and he would tell them to the General Staff. And Jakup Krasniqi also gave us whatever decisions or instructions the General Staff had for us. So the only person to do this was Jakup Krasniqi, to establish these links was Jakup Krasniqi who was the member of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... if we could know the meaning of the word toponym, which has been used three times, it was used in the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Place name. Topographical name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: It may be that. I wonder if the witness could be asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm not sure if that's what it is in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, there's a question about the word toponym, the word toponym. What do you mean by that word?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Toponym means the name that is given to a place or a village, which in this case is Klecka; it's name is Klecka. So it's -- I said that here we don't have to do with a command or something like that, but the name of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I say it's a great relief to have that answer because Defence bar seems to think that I should have known what that word meant. I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I have to acknowledge, it's the learning of Judge Van Den Wyngaert that helped me, so we stand together, topo nomo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sure Mr. Topolski will find some poetry that uses that word by tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, did you say in the interview that -- when you were talking about Klecka, did you ever say that you were talking about Jakup Krasniqi? Did you say that in the interview?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke about Klecka where the spokesperson of the KLA was established at the time, Jakup Krasniqi I mean, and when I speak about Klecka it's not about a command that was established there but it was the place where Jakup Krasniqi was interviewed and where he stayed for some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know in fact that Jakup Krasniqi did not stay in Klecka for very long but moved around to different places? Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that Jakup Krasniqi for a period -- he stayed in Klecka. He was in Javor. He also went to other villages such as Trpeze and other villages as well. But this was where we could communicate with him, and the period I'm speaking about, June, July, he was in Klecka until the middle of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I want you to look at the diagram and the names of the units that you've written on the diagram. Are you saying now that Jakup Krasniqi gave orders to those units that are on the diagram and that are below Klecka?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying that through Jakup Krasniqi we were conveyed orders by the General Staff. He was the only member of the General Staff that we knew and through which we could take orders of the General Staff. We could not take orders by people who we didn't know, whether they were members of the General Staff or not. And we could also send to him or convey to him our concerns or our notifications, whatever we had. And whatever the General Staff responded, he responded through Jakup Krasniqi -- sorry, the General Staff responded through Jakup Krasniqi to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Oh, so now you're saying the General Staff communicated through Jakup Krasniqi, not through Fatmir Limaj but through Jakup Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course not through Fatmir Limaj but through Jakup Krasniqi, who was a spokesperson of the General Staff and the only one we knew as such, as a member of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you see on the diagram that underneath Klecka you've written two names; you've written "Kumanova" and "Celiku."

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You did not write "Jakup Krasniqi," did you?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not write "Jakup Krasniqi" because it's written "General Staff" here. And I thought that in the person of Jakup Krasniqi was embodied the General Staff. So I saw -- I wrote only as a member of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But the General Staff is written above Klecka. At Klecka there's -- it's Kumanova and Celiku. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The location of Celiku, the meeting with Kumanova happened in Klecke. When I saw both of them when I went to Klecka. It means that Klecka was the place where Celiku and Jakup Krasniqi were staying at this period.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the -- you agree, do you not, that the positions that were positions or units that were established in these places in Luznica it was at the end of May or beginning of June, and Lapusnik was May or June, and Kroimire was in May. You agree with that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a rather long question. If you could break it up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I can. Let's take them one at a time. Luznica, the unit was established in May -- or you say "Luznica no doubt in May, end of May or beginning of June." That is correct, isn't it, when the unit was established there?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think that the formation of Luzhnice unit happened in this period. I wasn't sure whether it was created in May or June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And Lapusnik, as you say, is at the end of May or beginning -- no, I'm sorry, it was in May or June. End of May was Lapusnik. Right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought that in Lapusnik this happened at the end of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And Petrastica was in May?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pjetershtice couldn't be in May because the formation of the unit in Kroimire happened at the end of May. Petrastica might have been early July -- June or in the first half of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the -- you knew that there were two units in Lapusnik, Celiku 3 and Guri 3. That's what you say.

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that there were several units in Lapusnik, Celiku 3, Guri 3. If I'm not wrong there was also the Pellumbi and Lumi units. And I have said here -- I have written here also the Pellumbi unit. You could find it in -- on page 40 in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But when you're talking about Lapusnik in the interview, you only talked about Celiku 3 and Guri 3. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am talking as a region, I mean as a Lapusnik region the way I believed was the case. There was Pellumbi unit -- there was the village of Kizhareke and Lapusnik. I couldn't specify which villages there were, but I knew for sure that this unit operated in Kizhareke because it was near the unit that was created later in Nekovce.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Right. The Pellumbi unit was in Kishna Reka and it was on the other side of the Peja-Pristina road. Isn't that right? You knew that and you know that know. Right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't define the villages accurately because the division of the villages, Lapusnik, Kishna Reka, and Negrovce, and other villages of that region were -- had their houses there scattered there widely. So I couldn't know where one started and the other finished. So what I saw, that is that the unit Pellumbi was in Kishna Reka, I pointed that out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And with respect to Lapusnik, you said that the Celiku 3 Unit was on the Klecka side of the Peja-Pristina highway and the Guri 3 Unit was on the Drenica side of the Peja-Pristina highway, the other side of the Peja-Pristina highway. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was as I heard it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: SHUKRI BUJA [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that period, June/July.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a few minutes earlier, but I think it's a convenient point before I start another passage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We must adjourn now to resume tomorrow at 2.15. If I could ask you, Mr. Buja, to return then. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 8th day of March, 2005, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.57 p.m.,
